title: Reserve Country: Central Balkan Huts, Karst Caves and the Rhodope Vulture Gorges
subRegion: Central Balkan National Park (Stara Planina), the Lovech karst, and the Eastern Rhodopes

bestPeriod.window: late May to mid-June (waterfalls at full flow, vultures on eggs, meadows in flower)
bestPeriod.avoid: November–April on the ridge (Botev is a full winter mountain), and August in the Rhodopes (40 °C, rivers down to a trickle)

transport.note: €180–€300 (a hire car is effectively compulsory: €30–€45/day plus fuel)

activities.note: €40–€80 (Devetashka, Krushuna, Ökocentrum-style visitor centres, a guided vulture hide)

gatewayAirport: Sofia (SOF) or Plovdiv (PDV). Kalofer is 2 h from Sofia on the A1/I-6 via Karlovo. Finish near the Greek border: Madzharovo is 3 h 30 from Sofia, 2 h 15 from Plovdiv. Hire the car at the airport.
currency: Euro (EUR) — sole legal tender since 1 February 2026; mandatory dual BGN display ended 8 August 2026
summary: A week in the two wildest blocks of Bulgaria: a beech-and-granite national park where nine strict reserves are sealed off from everything but a marked footpath, and a semi-desert river gorge where griffon vultures…
hook: A week in the two wildest blocks of Bulgaria: a beech-and-granite national park where nine strict reserves are sealed off from everything but a marked footpath, and a semi-desert river gorge where griffon vultures ride the thermals over a rewilded valley. You sleep in unheated *hizha* bunkrooms at 1,800 m, drive forest roads that will take a hire car's sump off, and go two days without a signal. Not comfortable. Genuinely remote.

snapshot.Best period: Late May to mid-June, or September
snapshot.Getting there: Sofia (SOF) or Plovdiv (PDV). Kalofer is 2 h from Sofia on the A1/I-6 via Karlovo. Finish near the Greek border: Madzharovo is 3 h 30 from Sofia, 2 h 15 from Plovdiv. Hire the car at the airport.

itinerary.title: Kalofer and the highest waterfall in Bulgaria
itinerary.morning: Drive Sofia–Karlovo–**Kalofer**, the birthplace of Hristo Botev, and register your route intention at the **Central Balkan National Park** Kalofer information point [VERIFY: current Kalofer visitor point opening hours].
itinerary.afternoon: The Byala reka valley trail to **Raysko Praskalo** — "Paradise Spray" — which drops **124.5 m** in a single fall off the Botev cirque, the highest waterfall in Bulgaria and the Balkans. Full volume in late May, a thin thread by August.
itinerary.evening: Continue to **Hizha Rai** at roughly 1,950 m beneath the fall. Bean soup, a wood stove, a generator that dies at 22:00 [VERIFY: current Hizha Rai bed and half-board rates].

itinerary.title: Botev peak, 2,376 m
itinerary.morning: Leave at 06:30 for **Botev**, the Stara Planina's highest summit at **2,376 m**, crowned by an incongruous television mast and meteorological station. Two to three hours from Rai on marked trail, exposed to the ridge wind throughout.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the rim above **Dzhendema** reserve, the great south-facing wall of the range and the most strictly protected ground in Bulgaria. Look; do not enter.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Kalofer and drive the **Beklemeto (Troyan) pass** at about 1,525 m to a *vila* in **Cherni Osam** or **Apriltsi** — hot water, a real bed, and signal for the first time in 36 hours.

itinerary.title: Steneto and the beech forests
itinerary.morning: Up the Cherni Osam forest road to **Hizha Pleven** at about 1,300 m, gateway to the **Steneto** reserve — a Bulgarian component of UNESCO's *Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests* inscription of 2017.
itinerary.afternoon: The marked through-route into the Steneto gorge: limestone walls, the Cherni Osam river, caves in the flank, beech never cut. Marked trail only; the reserve permits nothing else.
itinerary.evening: Back down for the **Natural History Museum in Cherni Osam**, a serious taxidermy and habitat collection built by one family over decades [VERIFY: current Cherni Osam museum hours].

itinerary.title: Kozya Stena and the ridge huts
itinerary.morning: Park at the **Troyan Pass** monument on Beklemeto and walk the ridge west on **Kom–Emine** (E3) waymarks to **Kozya Stena** reserve, a narrow limestone crest holding Balkan endemics including edelweiss.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to **Hizha Kozya Stena** for soup, then across to **Hizha Dobrila** at roughly 1,800 m, the stone staging post on the ridge [VERIFY: current Hizha Dobrila rates and midweek staffing].
itinerary.evening: Stay at Dobrila. No signal, spring water, and the stars over the Steneto forest. Carry cash — there is no card machine on the ridge.

itinerary.title: Down to the karst: Devetashka and Krushuna
itinerary.morning: North to **Lovech** (about 1 h 15), then 20 km to **Devetaki** village and the **Devetashka Cave** — a colossal karst hall with seven ceiling openings and a floor the size of a stadium, holding a large bat colony. **Access is restricted in the bat breeding season, roughly June–July** [VERIFY: current Devetashka Cave seasonal closure dates and hours].
itinerary.afternoon: East to the **Krushuna waterfalls**, a travertine staircase of terraces and moss below the village — boardwalks, low gradient, and the busiest thing on this itinerary. Before 10:00 or after 16:00.
itinerary.evening: The long transfer south: Lovech to **Madzharovo** is roughly 290 km and 4 hours via Stara Zagora and Haskovo. Do it in daylight — the last hour is narrow gorge road.

itinerary.title: Vultures above the Arda
itinerary.morning: At first light, up to the viewpoint above the **Madzharovo** gorge on the Arda — the core breeding area of Bulgaria's **griffon vulture** colony and a last stronghold of the **Egyptian vulture**, the small migratory one that winters in Africa and is critically endangered in Europe.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Bulgarian Society for the Protection of Birds (BSPB/BDZP) Eastern Rhodopes Nature Conservation Centre** runs the field station, exhibition and guided hides. Book a hide in advance — it starts before dawn and there are few seats [VERIFY: current BSPB Madzharovo hide booking process and fee].
itinerary.evening: Stay at the centre. The old mining valley below is among the emptiest inhabited landscapes in the EU: black stork, sombre tit, and a river with nobody on it.

itinerary.title: Studen Kladenets and the Byala Reka wilderness
itinerary.morning: West along the Arda to the **Studen Kladenets** reservoir, focus of the Rhodope rewilding work — reintroduced **fallow and red deer** built up as a prey base for the vultures, and a feeding site above the water.
itinerary.afternoon: With high clearance and dry weather, run south into the **Byala Reka** basin towards Kroumovgrad: oak savanna, dry gorges, tortoises on the track, one of the least visited protected areas in the country. In a 2WD car on a wet day, do not.
itinerary.evening: Out via Kardzhali. Eat *patatnik*, drink Rhodope wine, and note that the week cost less than three nights in the Alps.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hizha Rai
accommodationStrategy.description: the only bed that puts you on Botev's rim at dawn instead of climbing 1,400 m from the valley. Wood stove, generator hours, spring water, bunkrooms.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone a few days ahead midweek, 2–3 weeks for a summer weekend. Cash only; bring a liner.

accommodationStrategy.name: Village *vila* rentals
accommodationStrategy.description: the midweek reset — hot water, drying space and a kitchen, 20 minutes from the Steneto trailhead and inside the Kom–Emine corridor. Wood-stove heating; ask whether wood is included.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–4 weeks ahead via Booking.com or direct with the owner. September is the tight month, because of the mushrooms.

accommodationStrategy.name: BSPB Eastern Rhodopes Nature Conservation Centre
accommodationStrategy.description: you sleep at the research station above the gorge, with the people who ring the birds. Simple rooms, shared facilities, exhibition on site, hides arranged at the desk.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct with BSPB well ahead for spring migration and the breeding season — the building is small [VERIFY: current BSPB Madzharovo room rates].

logistics.connectivity: A1 and Yettel cover Kalofer, Troyan, Apriltsi, Lovech and the Rhodope villages. There is **no signal at Hizha Rai, Hizha Dobrila or in the Steneto gorge** and patchy coverage on the Botev ridge. Download offline maps — Kom–Emine waymarks are good but sparse in cloud.
logistics.emergency: **112**, routing to the **Planinska spasitelna sluzhba** (Bulgarian Red Cross mountain rescue). Response to the Botev ridge is measured in hours. Leave your route with the hut warden and stick to it.
logistics.weather: The ridge makes its own weather. Botev is among the windiest points in Bulgaria and can go sun-to-whiteout in twenty minutes in any month; snow patches persist into June. The Rhodopes are the opposite problem — 40 °C and no shade in August.
logistics.bookingWindows: Huts, a few days to three weeks. The BSPB centre and any vulture hide, weeks to months in spring. The hire car as early as possible for September — Bulgarian fleets run out.
logistics.money: Bulgaria uses the **euro**, lev fixed at 1 EUR = 1.95583 BGN. **Every hut here is cash-only** and there is no ATM above the valley towns; carry €200–€250 in small notes. Cards work in Lovech, Troyan and Kardzhali.
logistics.transportRules: An electronic **vignette** is required on Bulgarian republican roads and motorways — buy it online or at a fuel station before driving. Check the rental agreement's unsurfaced-road exclusion. Fuel in Troyan and again in Haskovo; Rhodope stations are far apart and close early.
logistics.permits: No entry fee or permit for the national park. **Marked trails only in all nine reserves**; no camping or bivouac in reserves; camping only in designated park zones; **no open fires anywhere in the park**; no drones; dogs leashed and banned in reserves. Collecting plants, fungi or wood is prohibited in the core and reserves and permit-regulated elsewhere.

proTips: **Take Raysko Praskalo in the last week of May.** Snowmelt is what makes a 124 m waterfall look like one; by August it is a stain on a cliff.
**Phone the hut the day before, in Bulgarian if you can.** Wardens do not reliably answer email, and a hut listed as open may be shut for a week for supplies.

**Ask a Cherni Osam or Apriltsi host about mushrooms instead of searching alone.** Village knowledge of which slope is producing is decades deep, freely given, and keeps you legally outside the park core.
**Book the Madzharovo hide before anything else.** It is the one genuinely scarce thing here, and only the dawn session is worth doing.
**Use the Beklemeto pass as your bad-weather switch.** If the ridge is in cloud, drop north to Devetashka and Krushuna a day early and take Botev on the better morning.
**Carry 3 litres and a filter.** Kom–Emine ridge springs are reliable in June and unreliable in September; Rhodope tributaries in August are stagnant.
**Learn *"Има ли мечки тук?"*** — "are there bears here?" The answer is always yes, and the advice that follows beats anything written down.

raw.Access requirements: Three grades. **Asphalt throughout**: the Beklemeto (Troyan) pass road at ~1,525 m and the Kalofer approach. **Rough but 2WD-passable when dry**: the Cherni Osam forest road to **Hizha Pleven**, broken concrete then gravel, fine in a hatchback if you crawl. **High clearance genuinely required**: the upper forest road above Kalofer, the tracks around **Studen Kladenets**, and everything off tarmac in the **Byala Reka** basin, where the road is a dry riverbed with a name. Rain downgrades all three within an hour, and Bulgarian hire cars are almost always barred from unsurfaced roads — read the agreement.
raw.Isolation level: 4 of 5: Two nights in huts with no road access and no mains power; the Rhodope nights in a village of a few hundred with one shop. Not 5 — there is always a warden or a village within three hours' walk — but nowhere here is help fast.
raw.Wild camping vs bivouac — the distinctio: Bulgarian law prohibits camping outside designated sites, and inside **Central Balkan National Park** camping is allowed only at the directorate's **designated camping and bivouac zones**, mostly at or beside the huts. In practice a **bivouac** — one night, late in, early out, no established camp, no fire, pitched beside a hut or at a marked bivouac place — is accepted by wardens. A **camp** — several nights, a fire ring, gear spread out, off-zone — is not, and is fined. Inside the nine **strict reserves** (Boatin, Tsarichina, Kozya Stena, Steneto, Sokolna, Peeshtite Skali, Severen Dzhendem, Dzhendema, Stara Reka) there is **no camping and no bivouac at all**: the marked through-trail and nothing else — no leaving the path, no fire, no picking, no dogs, no drone [VERIFY: current Central Balkan NP bivouac zone list and seasonal reserve closures].
raw.Foraging: Medicinal plants fall under the **Medicinal Plants Act (Zakon za lechebnite rastenia)**: personal-quantity picking on state forest land is free, **commercial collection needs a municipal permit**, and several species are under annual quota or banned from wild collection outright — **Sideritis scardica** (*mursalski chay*) and **Rhodiola rosea** are the two you will be tempted by and must not take [VERIFY: current banned/quota species list]. Mushrooms — *manatarka* (cep), chanterelle — are free for personal use on state forest land in the Troyan and Apriltsi valleys, the classic September activity. **Inside the reserves and the park core, all collecting of plants, fungi and firewood is prohibited.**
raw.Bear and wolf protocol: The Central Balkan holds a resident **brown bear** population and the beech reserves are prime habitat. Make noise on blind bends and in dense beech, avoid dusk in berry season, never approach a cub, keep food out of the tent, and if you meet one do not run — back away facing it, talking level. Wolves are present in both ranges and are not a practical concern. The likelier problem is a livestock guardian dog at a *kolibi* sheepfold: stop, do not turn your back, let the shepherd call it off.
raw.Off-grid utilities: The high huts (Rai, Dobrila, Kozya Stena) run **generator or solar on fixed evening hours**, with wood stoves, spring water, dry toilets, cold showers, and are **cash-only**; blankets are provided, bedding often is not. Village *vila* rentals in Cherni Osam, Apriltsi and Ribaritsa have mains power and hot water but frequently no central heating, only a wood *pech* — ask before booking a May night.
